correctness.rationale: The likelihood-ratio transformation is exact. Normal Mills ratio gives the sharp endpoint power with its normal-tail logarithmic correction. Independent strata and a dominated truncation/oscillation argument reduce the entire underdispersed scaled error to a convergent centered unit-interval series. The first unit interval alone controls the sharp right Pareto tail; a convergent deterministic oscillation envelope bounds the rest. Potter bounds justify first-mean and, when the variance exceeds one half, second-mean passage, yielding the explicit series variance. Local power-log integrability gives the exact finite-grid p-moment boundary, including logarithmic divergence at equality. For the variance is at least one, bounded variation and continuity off the single indicator jump make all other cells negligible after multiplying by n, while the jump cell yields exactly the Bernoulli phase. The exact finite-grid raw Gaussian moment formulas were checked in the standalone package checker: 634 tests passed; these finite tests are not used as an infinite proof.

value.rationale: A fixed Gaussian upper-tail probability is a canonical rare-event numerical integral and one-evaluation-per-proposal-stratum is a natural unbiased variance-reduction design. The theorem identifies a qualitatively important proposal variance phase change: underdispersion produces a universal, threshold-independent heavy-tailed error law and possible infinite RMSE; at or above unit variance the jump cell forces an arithmetic, not Gaussian, asymptotic law. It supplies exact constants and a moment-existence threshold useful for assessing error bars and choosing safe proposals. This is a motivated complete 1D classification, not a slight coefficient tweak or a claim of unrestricted optimality.
